what_it_does: Serverless computing lets developers run small functions in the cloud without managing servers; the cloud provider automatically decides how much CPU and memory each function gets. When multiple functions are chained into a workflow (a directed acyclic graph, or DAG — a flowchart with no loops), existing systems assign CPU and memory together as a fixed bundle, which wastes resources when a function needs a lot of memory but little CPU, or vice versa. AARC decouples CPU and memory provisioning so each can be set independently, then solves the resulting enormous configuration search space by first identifying the critical path (the chain of steps that determines the total runtime) and prioritizing configuration effort there. It uses a scheduling algorithm borrowed from real-time systems to enforce response-time guarantees (called service-level objectives, or SLOs) while reducing wasted resources. The abstract suggests this cuts search time significantly, though details depend on the full paper.
